item.title: Government and Opposition agree Malta's economic model must evolve
item.description: Government and Opposition speakers agreed in parliament that Malta's economic model needs to evolve, with Economy Minister Silvio Schembri rejecting claims that the government lacked direction. Schembri said Malta Enterprise received 200 applications under the Invest scheme over the past year, representing €1.5 billion in proposed new investment, and announced the scheme would be extended by six months. PN shadow minister Michael Piccinino argued the Budget has no clear plan to transform the economic model, saying growth over 13 years was driven largely by population growth and that productivity per capita declined last year.
item.content:encoded:
Government and Opposition speakers agreed in parliament that Malta's economic model needs to evolve, with Economy Minister Silvio Schembri rejecting claims that the government lacked direction. Schembri said Malta Enterprise received 200 applications under the Invest scheme over the past year, representing €1.5 billion in proposed new investment, and announced the scheme would be extended by six months. PN shadow minister Michael Piccinino argued the Budget has no clear plan to transform the economic model, saying growth over 13 years was driven largely by population growth and that productivity per capita declined last year.

Sources: Times of Malta

item.title: Bomb-making instructions and ISIS material found in terrorism suspect's possession
item.description: Police investigating 21-year-old Daniel Spiteri told the court that they found notebooks with bomb-making instructions and recruitment tactics, along with two mobile phones, 12 pen drives and a laptop seized from his residence. Officer Zachary Zammit of the anti-terrorism unit said YouTube searches included extremist preachers linked to ISIS inspiration, and that Spiteri is believed to have travelled to Syria for terrorist training. Seven more people were arrested in connection with the ongoing investigation, and Spiteri faces several terrorism-related charges before Magistrate Ann Marie Thake.

item.title: PN leader invites artists to open discussion after culture minister row
item.description: Opposition leader Alex Borg announced a public discussion for Malta's cultural and creative sectors, to be held at the Mediterranean College of Sports in Birkirkara on Sunday, 15 November at 11am. The move follows Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea's remarks describing his first four months in office as "traumatic", questioning artists' reliance on public funding and saying creativity must operate within certain "norms". Prime Minister Robert Abela has said the minister's comments were insensitive. More than 2,100 people have signed a letter calling for the minister's resignation.

item.title: Accommodation tops tourist complaints in Malta
item.description: The Malta Tourism Authority received 1,182 complaints between January 2025 and October 2026, Tourism Minister Jo Etienne Abela told parliament. Accommodation and lodging accounted for 162 complaints, followed by consumer rights and prices with 141. Customer service and staff conduct drew 123 complaints, while 113 concerned licensing and 107 safety and personal security.

item.title: Residents urged to object to apartment complex in Paola's conservation area
item.description: Moviment Graffitti urged residents to object to a proposed 23-unit residential development in Paola's Urban Conservation Area, warning it would threaten the historic character of the locality and worsen traffic congestion. The plan would replace existing houses and gardens with two maisonettes, 12 apartments, eight penthouses and a house. Objections can be submitted to the Planning Authority.

item.title: New York contingent: financial information still being gathered
item.description: More than a month after a Maltese contingent travelled to New York for the UN General Assembly, the financial details of the trip have still not been published despite repeated parliamentary questions. Shadow Minister Michael Piccinino has asked twice for the information, and the President's Office said data on the delegation's size, roles and total cost is still being gathered, including travel, accommodation and transport expenses.

item.title: BOV webinar helps businesses navigate international sanctions
item.description: Bank of Valletta hosted a webinar for businesses on understanding international sanctions, warning signs and financial crime prevention. The session covered how sanctions can affect payments, supplier relations and client verification, and offered practical guidance on managing risk and making informed international business decisions.

item.title: 14-year-old boy out of intensive care after Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq boat crash
item.description: The 14-year-old boy involved in the boat crash on the yellow rock off Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq has been moved out of the intensive care unit at Mater Dei Hospital after improving in recent hours. His father Keith Caruana, 48, from Il-Mellieħa, died shortly after reaching hospital, and Daniel Buttigieg, 44, from Bormla, remains under care.

item.title: €3 Temu duty set to be replaced from 2028, von der Leyen tells Agius
item.description: The controversial €3 customs duty on low-value online purchases from platforms such as Temu and Shein is expected to be replaced by a different system from July 2028, according to a letter from European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to Maltese MEP Peter Agius. She confirmed the flat-rate duty is temporary, pending the EU's reformed customs system and a new EU Customs Data Hub, and clarified legal responsibility for paying the duty falls on platforms and operators rather than consumers.

item.title: Maltese MEP leads EU push for transparent flight and ferry bookings
item.description: Maltese MEP Daniel Attard has been appointed to lead European Parliament negotiations on new rules for online travel booking platforms, aimed at making price comparisons, sponsored results and final costs clearer for travellers. Attard said the proposals are particularly relevant for Malta and Gozo, where air and sea connections are essential. The legislation is still under discussion at EU level and has not been approved.

item.title: Creative Europe MEDIA opens funding call for Maltese creative talent
item.description: Local film producers, game developers and audio-visual professionals are being urged to apply for a new round of European funding, with the Creative Europe Programme's MEDIA strand having opened calls for 2027. The funding covers narrative video games, immersive technology, film distribution, television and documentary production, offering international support and cross-border collaboration for Maltese talent.

item.title: Scientists push back on culture minister's remarks
item.description: The Malta Chamber of Scientists has distanced itself from Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea's comments on artistic expression, insisting that scientific progress, like artistic expression, depends on challenging established norms and questioning authority. The chamber's intervention follows a leaked audio recording in which the minister described his first four months in office as "traumatic" and questioned artists' reliance on public funding.

item.title: Vatican bank wins Malta case but faces €21.5m bill in Budapest
item.description: Nine years after the Vatican bank took a Malta-based fund to court over a crumbling Budapest palace, Judge Mark Simiana ordered four investment companies, two in Malta and two in Luxembourg, to pay the bank €24.1 million for breaching duties of loyalty. The judgment follows a debt-laden palace that Luxembourg fund managers pitched to the bank.
